# kaya-publications Specification

## Purpose
The client-facing half of kaya: publications that answer a visitor's questions
instead of mirroring the internal record. Twelve reader-facing products are
composed over the eleven document kinds, collections group related information,
and packages bundle products for a purpose. Keeping the three tiers apart
prevents the two failure modes the origin investigation found — dozens of
overlapping templates, and stub pages that exist because a taxonomy said so
rather than because there is information to publish.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Publication tiers

A publication SHALL carry exactly one tier — product, collection, or package —
drawn from that tier's closed vocabulary; a package SHALL list products, a
collection SHALL list products or documents, and an unknown tier or name SHALL
be refused with a labeled error naming the offered value. The three
vocabularies are pinned by the "Tier vocabularies are closed" scenario.

#### Scenario: Product and package composed

- **WHEN** a `project-site` package lists `overview` and `reference`
- **THEN** the package builds as navigation over those two products and
  embeds neither product's content

#### Scenario: Package cannot list a family

- **WHEN** a package lists `exploration.experiment-record` as a member
- **THEN** the build refuses with a labeled error naming the family reference
  and the package tier

#### Scenario: Unknown product refused

- **WHEN** a publication declares product `experiment-report`
- **THEN** the build refuses with a labeled error naming `experiment-report`
  and lists the closed product vocabulary

#### Scenario: Tier vocabularies are closed

- **WHEN** the publication tier vocabularies are inspected
- **THEN** the product tier admits exactly overview, getting-started, tutorial,
  how-to, concept, reference, example, troubleshooting, faq,
  status-compatibility, release-migration, architecture-design; the collection
  tier admits exactly glossary, example-gallery, api-catalogue,
  capability-catalogue, compatibility-matrix, feature-index, knowledge-index,
  related-projects, topic-map; and the package tier admits exactly project-site,
  developer-guide, user-guide, api-documentation, integration-guide,
  research-background, ai-knowledge-package, offline-bundle

### Requirement: Composition without duplication

A product SHALL be composed from document-family references, a package SHALL reference its member products rather than embedding their content, and each fact SHALL appear once in a published tree with cross-references elsewhere.

#### Scenario: Shared fact rendered once

- **WHEN** two products in one package compose the same
  `orientation.project-overview` document
- **THEN** the fact appears once and the second product cross-references it

#### Scenario: Package embeds no product body

- **WHEN** a package is assembled
- **THEN** its generated block contains only member names and links, never a
  product's rendered body

### Requirement: Justified emission

A product SHALL be emitted only when at least one admissible backing document exists; a product without backing information SHALL be omitted and reported, and no publication tree SHALL contain a stub page for it.

#### Scenario: No stub page

- **WHEN** no document is admissible for product `tutorial`
- **THEN** no tutorial page is written and the build summary reports
  `tutorial` as omitted with reason `no-backing-document`

#### Scenario: Omission visible in the package

- **WHEN** a package lists an omitted product
- **THEN** the package's navigation names it as unavailable rather than
  linking to a page that does not exist

### Requirement: Reader-question binding

Each product SHALL declare exactly one reader question from its fixed binding,
and a document included in a product SHALL be admissible for that product per
the admission table; both bindings are pinned by the "Every product declares a
question" scenario.

#### Scenario: Inadmissible inclusion refused

- **WHEN** product `faq` includes `exploration.experiment-specification`
- **THEN** the build refuses with a labeled error naming the product, the
  kind, and the admission table row

#### Scenario: Every product declares a question

- **WHEN** a publication tree is built
- **THEN** each emitted product names its reader question, fixed as: overview —
  what is this and why does it matter; getting-started — how do I reach a first
  result; tutorial — can you teach me through a guided outcome; how-to — how do
  I accomplish this task; concept — why does it work this way; reference — what
  exactly is this; example — what can I do with it; troubleshooting — why is
  this broken and how do I fix it; faq — what do people keep asking;
  status-compatibility — what can I rely on; release-migration — what changed
  and what must I do; architecture-design — how is it structured and why
- **AND** the documents admitted to each product are exactly: overview ←
  orientation.project-overview; getting-started ← orientation.project-overview,
  reuse-handoff.reproduction-package; tutorial ← exploration.experiment-record,
  exploration.exploration-brief; how-to ← reuse-handoff.technical-reference,
  reuse-handoff.reproduction-package; concept ← understanding.decision-record,
  understanding.findings-and-analysis; reference ←
  reuse-handoff.technical-reference, orientation.research-map; example ←
  exploration.experiment-record; troubleshooting ←
  understanding.findings-and-analysis; faq ← understanding.findings-and-analysis,
  understanding.decision-record; status-compatibility ←
  orientation.project-overview, exploration.experiment-record;
  release-migration ← orientation.project-overview,
  understanding.decision-record; architecture-design ←
  understanding.decision-record, orientation.research-map

### Requirement: One source, many formats

Every delivery format of a publication tree SHALL be projected from the same document source and source map; no format SHALL be maintained separately, and every fact published in any format SHALL be attributable to the same event ids.

#### Scenario: Markdown and export agree

- **WHEN** a publication tree is rendered to Markdown and to its structured
  export
- **THEN** every fact in the export traces to the same event ids as its
  Markdown counterpart

#### Scenario: No separately maintained format

- **WHEN** a delivery format is requested twice from unchanged inputs
- **THEN** both outputs are byte-identical and neither required hand edits

### Requirement: Property coverage mirror

Every property row in the layer sidecar SHALL be verified by exactly one dedicated scenario.

#### Scenario: tier_resolved

- **WHEN** a publication declares a tier and a name
- **THEN** the pair resolves to exactly one tier vocabulary entry or is refused
- **VERIFIES** [[kaya.publications.tier_resolved]]

#### Scenario: fact_once

- **WHEN** a package and its products are built from one document graph
- **THEN** each fact body appears once and elsewhere only as a reference
- **VERIFIES** [[kaya.publications.fact_once]]

#### Scenario: stub_free

- **WHEN** a product has no admissible backing document
- **THEN** no page is written and the omission is reported
- **VERIFIES** [[kaya.publications.stub_free]]

#### Scenario: inadmissible_refused

- **WHEN** a product includes a document kind outside its admission row
- **THEN** the build refuses with a label naming product, kind, and row
- **VERIFIES** [[kaya.publications.inadmissible_refused]]

#### Scenario: format_attribution

- **WHEN** two delivery formats are projected from the same source
- **THEN** both trace every fact to the same event ids
- **VERIFIES** [[kaya.publications.format_attribution]]

# kaya.publications — dual-format layer (sidecar)

## Purpose

The client-facing half of kaya's scope: publications that answer a visitor's
questions rather than mirror the internal record. Twelve reader-facing
products sit over the eleven document kinds; collections group related
information; packages bundle products for a purpose. Keeping the three tiers
apart is what prevents the two failure modes the origin investigation found:
dozens of overlapping templates, and stub pages that exist because a taxonomy
said so rather than because there is information to publish.

## Constraints

| id                        | kind      | expr                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | traces_to |
|---------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| tier_separated            | invariant | `every publication is exactly one of product, collection or package from the closed vocabularies; packages list products, collections list products or documents; an unknown tier or name is a labeled refusal`                | [[kaya.publications.layer]] |
| composition_no_duplication| invariant | `products compose document-family references and packages reference products; each fact body appears once in a published tree, elsewhere only as a cross-reference`                                                            | [[kaya.publications.layer]] |
| justified_emission        | invariant | `a product is emitted only when at least one admissible backing document exists; otherwise it is omitted and reported, and no stub page is written`                                                                            | [[kaya.publications.layer]] |
| reader_question_bound     | invariant | `each product declares exactly one reader question and admits only the document kinds in its admission row; an inadmissible inclusion is a labeled refusal naming product, kind and row`                                       | [[kaya.publications.layer]] |
| single_source_multi_format| invariant | `every delivery format is projected from the same document source and source map; no format is maintained separately and every fact traces to the same event ids in every format`                                              | [[kaya.publications.layer]] |

## Model

### States
- `selected`
- `composed`
- `emitted`
- `omitted`

### Transitions

| id       | from      | to       | guard                                                                                                                         |
|----------|-----------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| select   | selected  | composed | [[kaya.publications.layer.tier_separated]] ∧ [[kaya.publications.layer.reader_question_bound]]                                  |
| compose  | composed  | emitted  | [[kaya.publications.layer.composition_no_duplication]] ∧ [[kaya.publications.layer.single_source_multi_format]]                  |
| omit     | composed  | omitted  | ¬`backing document exists` ∧ [[kaya.publications.layer.justified_emission]]                                                     |

## Properties

| id                         | kind | derives_from                                          | generator                                  | predicate                                                   |
|----------------------------|------|-------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| tier_resolved              | unit | [[kaya.publications.layer.tier_separated]]             | `publication_with_unknown_tier()`          | `one tier resolved ∨ labeled refusal`                        |
| fact_once                  | unit | [[kaya.publications.layer.composition_no_duplication]] | `package_with_shared_fact()`               | `body occurrences == 1 ∧ others are references`               |
| stub_free                  | unit | [[kaya.publications.layer.justified_emission]]         | `product_without_backing_document()`       | `no page written ∧ omission reported`                        |
| inadmissible_refused       | unit | [[kaya.publications.layer.reader_question_bound]]      | `product_with_inadmissible_kind()`         | `labeled refusal naming product ∧ kind ∧ row`                 |
| format_attribution         | unit | [[kaya.publications.layer.single_source_multi_format]] | `two_formats_from_one_source()`            | `∀ fact: same event ids in both formats`                      |

## Requirements
### Requirement: Layer sidecar contract

This sidecar is the dual-format layer for the `kaya.publications` capability and SHALL be deployed verbatim by the archive companion; the plain delta in `spec.md` beside it is its openspec face.

#### Scenario: Archive deploys the layer

- **WHEN** the change `add-document-taxonomy` is archived after its scenarios
  have executing contract tests
- **THEN** the capability deploys with this layer attached fail-closed
